svg.title: Forward-Backward vs Viterbi
svg.desc: Forward-backward returns posterior probabilities date by date; Viterbi returns the single regime sequence with the highest joint probability over the span. The two can disagree.
svg.text: Regime probabilities at each date vs the single most likely path over the whole span
Joint probability of the whole path
A single path cannot express it
You get sequences that leave a regime and immediately return
Looks at the whole path to keep one date consistent
Staying is more likely than leaving and returning
Multiply the two to get γ
Probabilities for every date come out in one pass
Keep only the maximum in the lattice, then backtrack
Only one survivor per node, so the path is unique
Forward-backward gives the probability at each date; Viterbi gives the single most likely sequence.
Use forward-backward when you need regime probabilities, Viterbi when you need a label sequence.
but there is no guarantee it is the optimal path
Next: learning transitions and emissions from data — Baum-Welch vs Bayesian.
